name: Seguimiento comercial con IA - Diseña campañas para tus clientes.
description:
Muchas empresas acumulan contactos interesados, propuestas pendientes y clientes con los que han perdido el contacto. Dar seguimiento a esas relaciones requiere organización, contexto y mensajes que lleguen en el momento adecuado.

En este encuentro online veremos **cómo diseñar y ejecutar campañas de seguimiento de preventa y postventa con IA, y convertirlas en un servicio que puedas ofrecer a tus clientes.**
Trabajaremos con ejemplos de seguimiento de propuestas, recuperación de oportunidades, acompañamiento tras la compra y reactivación de clientes.

Recorreremos tanto el diseño de la campaña como los datos, la configuración del correo y los aspectos legales que debes revisar antes de activarla.

## Qué veremos

* Cómo identificar oportunidades de seguimiento en la base de leads y clientes de una empresa.
* Cómo diferenciar campañas de **preventa, postventa, reactivación y recompra.**
* Cómo segmentar contactos según su relación con el negocio, sus necesidades y sus interacciones anteriores.
* Cómo definir el objetivo, el mensaje, la frecuencia y las condiciones de salida de cada campaña.
* Qué aspectos revisar sobre **RGPD, LSSI, permisos de contacto y solicitudes de baja.**
* Cómo preparar dominios y buzones y qué papel tienen **SPF, DKIM y DMARC.**
* Cómo abordar el calentamiento de buzones y el volumen de envío según el caso, y cómo interpretar rebotes y quejas de spam.
* Cómo utilizar IA para preparar mensajes personalizados y secuencias con revisión humana.
* Cómo conectar las campañas con el CRM, gestionar respuestas y detener el seguimiento cuando corresponda.
* Cómo medir resultados: respuestas, oportunidades recuperadas, conversiones y recompra.
* Cómo convertir este proceso en un servicio con alcance, precio y responsabilidades definidos.
* Un framework práctico: **objetivo → segmento → datos y permisos → mensajes → ejecución → seguimiento → resultados.**

name: Closing the Continuous Learning Loop: From Agent Traces to Agent Training
description:
**Zoom link**: [https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562](https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562)

**Talk #0: Introductions and Meetup Updates**
by Chris Fregly and Antje Barth

**Talk #1: Closing the Continuous Learning Loop: From Agent Traces to Agent Training**
by Rustem Feyzkhanov, Engineering Manager @ Snorkel.ai
Production traces show where agents fail, but how do we turn those failures into learning? This talk explores a practical loop from traces to reproducible simulations, verifiable rewards, and model improvement through fine-tuning or reinforcement learning. We’ll also look at when it’s better to change prompts, tools, or the agent harness instead of updating model weights.

name: Sept 24 - AI, ML and Computer Vision Meetup
description:
Join our virtual meetup on September 24 to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Date, Time and Location**

Sep 24, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-september-24-2026)**

**How Do Mercedes-Benz AI Principles Drive our Innovation?**

At Mercedes-Benz, our AI Principles guide every step of innovation, emphasizing responsible use, safety and reliability, explainability, and the protection of privacy. These principles go beyond statements and actively shape how we design, test, and deploy AI systems in real-world automotive and enterprise settings. In this talk, I will present how these principles inspired our recent research on when reusing LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) is effective. By combining theoretical analysis with synthetic data as a proxy for enterprise scenarios, we uncovered the strengths and limitations of modular AI components under constrained data access. Our findings provide practical guidance on when reused LoRAs could deliver high-quality results.

*About the Speaker*

[Mei-Yen Chen](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mei-yen-chen-22937787) is a Senior Data Scientist at Mercedes-Benz Tech Innovation GmbH in Germany with 10 years of industry experience in AI and data solutions. She leads early-stage AI projects across business functions and collaborates with research institutions on machine learning and responsible AI.

**Region Tokens as the Visual Primitive: From Recognition to World Modeling**

Patch-based tokenization has become the default interface between vision encoders and downstream models, yet patches carry no semantic structure and scale poorly with resolution and temporal extent. This talk presents a research program centered on replacing patch tokens with region-level representations — semantically dense tokens grounded in visual entities rather than arbitrary grid crops.

I will describe RELOCATE, REN, and T-REN, a progression of methods that produce region tokens via pooling, train them with region-level objectives, and extend them to video with temporal coherence. I will then present ongoing work integrating region tokens into VLMs to directly expand visual context capacity, and preliminary results on future region trajectory prediction as a foundation for world modeling.

The broader thesis is that region-level tokens are a more natural unit of visual computation than patches, and their advantage compounds as task complexity, resolution, and temporal horizon increase.

*About the Speaker*

[Savya Khosla](https://www.linkedin.com/in/savyakhosla/) is a second-year Ph.D. student at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, advised by Prof. Derek Hoiem and Prof. Alex Schwing.

**Leveraging Text-To-Image Diffusion Models for Consistent Set-to-Set Generation**

Image collections are humans' primary way of capturing the world, yet advances in generative editing remain largely inapplicable to this modality. We address this gap by introducing Match-and-Fuse - a zero-shot, training-free method for consistent set-to-set generation from image collections that share a common visual element but differ in viewpoint, capture time, and surrounding content.
Our key idea is a unified graph-based framework that combines dense correspondences with an emergent prior in text-to-image diffusion models to generate coherent canvases. We achieve state-of-the-art consistency and visual quality, and unlock new creative capabilities for content generation.

*About the Speaker*

[Kate Feingold](https://www.linkedin.com/in/katefeingold/) is a PhD student in Computer Vision at the Weizmann Institute of Science. Her research sits at the intersection of generative models, 3D/4D perception, and multimodal learning, focusing on problems where vision meets other modalities or paradigms in creative tasks.

**Yield Estimation of a Coffee in a dense environment**

This presentation provides a detailed workflow related to coffee yield estimation in a dense environment. With photos of pre-harvest coffee plants from a couple of coffee estates, details related to pre-processing, annotation to detect regions of interest (ROI), object detection training and inferencing results with various Yolo models and finally segmentation with SAM2 and Yolo\*-seg with training and inference results to determine the count of raw, pre-mature, mature and over-mature coffee berries and finally the yield of the entire estate. All this is based on real world data captured on iPhone and android phones.

*About the Speaker*

[Raghu M. Rao](http://www.linkedin.com/in/raghumrao) is a consultant working on applications of computer vision AI models. He was previously with AMD and Xilinx. He has a Ph.D. in Wireless Communications from UCLA and is a Senior Member, IEEE. His current interests are in applications of AI for agriculture, health care and wireless communications.

Stop doing this manually.
In this workshop, you'll customize and deploy a working AI research agent in 3 hours. Fork an existing competitive intelligence agent, wire in your own data sources (RSS feeds, APIs, whatever's available), and run it. Feed it a company or industry keyword. Get back structured intelligence: recent news, hiring patterns, market positioning, gaps, red flags.

* Clone a working competitive intelligence agent from GitHub

* Test it live on a real company or competitor

name: Sept 30 - Building Composable Vision Workflows in FiftyOne
description:
This workshop explores the [FiftyOne](https://docs.voxel51.com/index.html) plugin framework to build custom computer vision applications. You’ll learn to extend the FiftyOne App with Python based panels and server side operators, as well as integrate external tools for labeling, vector search, and model inference into your dataset views.

**Date, Time and Location**

Sep 30, 2026
9 AM - 10 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/building-composable-vision-workflows-in-fiftyone-september-30-2026)**

You’ll also automate repetitive tasks by writing custom workflows executing within the FiftyOne environment. Attendees will learn to transform FiftyOne from a visualization tool into a central hub for your vision stack.

What you'll learn:

* **Build Python plugins.** Define plugin manifests and directory structures to register custom functionality within the FiftyOne ecosystem.
* **Develop server side operators.** Write functions to execute model inference, data cleaning, or metadata updates from the App interface.
* **Build interactive panels.** Create custom UI dashboards using to visualize model metrics or specialized dataset distributions.
* **Manage operator execution contexts.** Pass data between the App front end and your backend to build dynamic user workflows.
* **Implement delegated execution.** Configure background workers to handle long running data processing tasks without blocking the user interface.
* **Build labeling integrations.** Streamline the flow of data between FiftyOne and annotation platforms through custom triggers and ingestion scripts.
* **Extend vector database support.** Program custom connectors for external vector stores to enable semantic search across large sample datasets.
* **Package and share plugins.** Distribute your extensions internally and externally

name: Open Source Climate Accounting: What Exists, What's Missing+Where To Contribute
description:
Climate accounting increasingly depends on systems that were never designed to work together. Registries use different standards and data models. The same activity can appear across multiple systems. Measurement data may come from sensors, satellite observations, models, or manual reporting, often with limited provenance or no straightforward way for downstream users to verify how a claim was produced.

These are not only reporting problems but they are problems of interoperability, provenance, reconciliation and trust between independent systems.

A substantial amount of open-source work already exists to address them, but much of it remains fragmented or little known outside the communities that built it. This session will map that landscape: what is already available, what is mature enough to use today, what remains experimental and where meaningful technical contributions are still needed.

The aim is not to argue that blockchain is the answer to climate accounting. It is to look practically at where distributed ledgers, verifiable data, open standards and other open-source infrastructure can solve specific problems or where they cannot.

Structure - The session would begin with a short framing of the technical problems behind climate and impact accounting: provenance, reconciliation, double counting, interoperability and verification across organisational boundaries.

From there, members of the LF Decentralized Trust community could walk through existing open-source projects and frameworks, explaining what they were built to solve, how mature they are and where they are being used today.

The final part would focus on the gaps: problems that remain unsolved, areas where maintainers would welcome contributions and practical ways for developers, researchers and organisations to get involved.

The IEEE ClimateChain Global Hackathon ([https://ieee-climatechain-hack.devpost.com/](https://ieee-climatechain-hack.devpost.com/)) would be introduced as one of those routes to contribution.

The goal is for participants to leave with a clearer picture of what already exists, which problems are genuinely open and where their time and technical skills could have the greatest value.

name: From Counter.Inc() to a billion series
description:
Add a counter. Two lines and you can finally see how often your service fails.

Then you add a label to tell failure reasons apart and the counter becomes genuinely useful. You can now see why it's failing.
So you start adding more labels, one for the kind of user, one for the value of the operation. Each one seems reasonable and enables rich queries and alerts.

This talk follows that counter all the way down: from instrumenting a Go service, to how Prometheus scrapes and stores your data, to building a horizontally scalable distributed metrics database as you go from just one counter to billions of them.

You don't need to know anything about observability to attend this session!
